svg.title: stdx's regular expressions on rebar's curated set against Rust's regex and Go's regexp, on AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor
svg.desc: rebar's curated searches, in multiples of Rust regex's speed: against Rust regex: ahead on 23 (1 inside 5%), level on 0, behind on 8 of 31 rows, 31 patterns; geometric mean over these rows 1.10; from 0.58 to 1.73; against Go regexp: ahead on 30, level on 0, behind on 1 of 31. rebar's curated compiles, in multiples of Rust regex's speed: against Rust regex: ahead on 9, level on 0, behind on 1 of 10 rows, 10 patterns; geometric mean over these rows 3.50; from 0.92 to 8.35; against Go regexp: ahead on 8, level on 0, behind on 2 of 10.
svg.text: stdx's regular expressions on rebar's curated set against Rust's regex and Go's regexp, on AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor
The median of 10 jobs on AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor, the CPU model of 10 of 18 jobs, the most of any: runs
The bars share one logarithmic axis of stdx over Rust regex. The other libraries stand in the columns at the right.
A bar is the median of stdx over Rust regex:
|—| the interval of the median: the jobs' 2nd lowest to 2nd highest ratio, 98% confidence
the median of another CPU model's jobs: INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8573C (2), AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor (2), AMD
rebar's curated searches, in multiples of Rust regex's speed
against Rust regex: ahead on 23 (1 inside 5%), level on 0, behind on 8 of 31 rows, 31 patterns; geometric mean over these rows 1.10; from
against Go regexp: ahead on 30, level on 0, behind on 1 of 31
Each row is a benchmark of rebar's curated set whose engines name Go's regexp or RE2, under rebar's own model, pattern and haystack. No
claim of stdx is judged on these rows. rebar's author also wrote Rust's crate, and rebar's BIAS.md says the set may favor that crate.
rebar's curated compiles, in multiples of Rust regex's speed
against Rust regex: ahead on 9, level on 0, behind on 1 of 10 rows, 10 patterns; geometric mean over these rows 3.50; from 0.92 to 8.35
against Go regexp: ahead on 8, level on 0, behind on 2 of 10
A row is ahead or behind where its interval lies above or below 1, and level where it holds 1 inside 5% of 1. A row whose interval holds 1
and reaches past 5% is unclear: its jobs do not settle it. A difference inside 5% is one this chart calls too small to matter, and the
The columns at the right are stdx's speed over another library's, the median of the jobs. A library has no speed (—) on a pattern that it
refuses, where its answer is not Go regexp's, and where it has no such call.
stdx timed again, last in each round, differed from stdx timed first by at most 21.9% in any job of any row.
On another CPU model, these rows fall on the other side of 1: 02-literal-alternate/sherlock-ru (AMD EPYC 9V74 80-Core Processor, 0.74);
